title: Gid's Island Fort
summary: Gid's Island Fort is remembered through nineteenth-century local history rather than through a clearly preserved archaeological site. Benjamin F. Thompson mentioned the North Fork fort in his 1843 History of Long Island, making Thompson's account important but limited by the perspective of later writers.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Corchaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: Documented in nineteenth-century historical accounts, the earthen remains of the Gideon's Island Indian Fort once stood on a sandy accumulation of land connected to modern-day Orient 9 10 . Preserving the memory of these coastal fortifications demonstrates that early Native communities actively built substantial defensive structures to protect their strategic territories and manage shifting regional trade networks.
